subject: Pilot: temporary residency & staggered wipe — SLA language
thread_messages:
From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@lumenhealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement LumenHealth <procurement@lumenhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Temporary residency for pilot + staggered wipe questions

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looks promising for our prototype. A couple of legal / procurement asks came up from my side that we need to lock in before we roll the pilot into our sandbox environment:

- Can Redwood support a temporary residency window for pilot data that is shorter than your standard 90/180 day templates? We're looking at a 30-day residency for model inputs, with an optional 90-day audit hold that we can toggle per environment.
- We need a staggered wipe: first a deprecation of KV cache and model-context after 30 days, then a full account-level wipe (including backups) after 120 days. Is that achievable and auditable?
- For legal, we need a clear deletion certification step that we can receive after wipe completion.

If you can share proposed SLA/order form language and any flow diagrams, that would help speed procurement. We have a small pilot budget (deal LH-2026-033) and would like to get this into an order form next week if possible.

Best,
Alicia Torres
Sr. Product Manager (AI)
LumenHealth

Hi Alicia — great to connect.

Short answers up front: yes, we can support a 30-day pilot residency with an opt-in 90-day audit hold, and we can implement a two-stage wipe (cache/context first; backups and persistent stores after). We'll provide a deletion certification PDF once the wipe completes.

I'm looping in Naomi (Policy & Order Forms) and Vivek (Customer Ops) to propose precise SLA wording and to confirm the operational steps for the staggered wipe and certification.

Attached: preliminary SLA appendix (pilot_sla_draft_v1.pdf) showing proposed language and timeboxes. Also included a simple flow diagram (data_removal_flow.png).

Two quick clarifications so we align the order form:
1) Does Lumen want the 90-day audit hold to be controllable per-environment or per-deal? (We can do either; per-environment is slightly more operational work.)
2) For backups: do you require immediate physical zeroing of backups on completion or is cryptographic irrecoverability (re-encryption and key destruction) acceptable?

If you confirm those, Naomi will translate into order form clauses.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Temporary residency for pilot + staggered wipe questions

Alex / Vivek — first pass below; I drafted language intended for inclusion as an SLA appendix and order-form callout. I'm fine to tighten wording based on Lumen legal feedback.

Proposed SLA appendix (high level):
- Pilot Data Residency: Redwood will host LumenHealth pilot data in the US region for a temporary residency window of thirty (30) calendar days following ingestion.
- Audit Hold: LumenHealth may elect an Audit Hold for specific environments within the pilot. When enabled, Audit Hold extends the retention of model inputs and derived logs by an additional ninety (90) calendar days beyond the residency window. Audit Hold is toggled via the Redwood Console and will be recorded in activity logs.
- Staggered Deletion Process:
  - Phase 1 (Day 30): Redwood will invalidate and purge in-memory caches and ephemeral model context (including KV cache and session history) within 72 hours of the residency window end. Deleted items will be marked in the internal purge index.
  - Phase 2 (Day 120): Redwood will perform account-level permanent deletion from primary storage and long-term backups. Backup deletion may be implemented via cryptographic key destruction unless LumenHealth explicitly requires physical overwrite.
- Deletion Certification: Upon completion of Phase 2, Redwood will provide a signed deletion certification containing: list of logical identifiers (non-sensitive), deletion timestamps, and confirmation of backup remediation steps. Certification will be delivered via the Redwood Console and can be emailed to procurement contact.
- Exceptions: Regulatory holds triggered by lawful process will pause deletion; Redwood will notify LumenHealth within 72 hours and provide remediation pathways.

Operational notes:
- Per-environment audit hold adds operational tagging; if Lumen opts for per-deal only, we can simplify the console controls and billing footprint.
- For cryptographic deletion we will log key destruction events to the customer audit trail.

Attached draft snippets are in redwood-sla-appendix.txt.

Vivek, can you confirm the 72-hour purge window for Phase 1 and that our standard backup retention/rotation supports a Day 120 permanent deletion with key rotation?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Policy & Order Forms Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): redwood-sla-appendix.txt

Alex / Naomi — this looks good and aligns with our internal expectations. A couple of minor asks before we finalize the order form:

1) Please make Audit Hold configurable per-environment (we will use it selectively across dev/stage/prod sandboxes).
2) For backup remediation, LumenHealth prefers cryptographic destruction as primary, but we need the option to request physical overwrite within the first 30 days post-pilot at additional cost; please include optional language and a pricing placeholder.

If you can send a tightened order-form clause (two short paragraphs) reflecting the above and the deletion certification stub, we can route to legal. Once legal signs off we'll prepare a PO against LH-2026-033.

Thanks — Alicia

Procurement reference: PO will reference deal LH-2026-033 and pilot dates.
